title: world protocol — records
description: The four things an entry in a document's `entities` array can be: a declaration introducing an entity, a patch modifying one an earlier layer declared, an override replacing components of a derived one, or a suppression deleting either. A record's shape is its kind — an `id` declares, a `derivation` reaches a derived entity, `suppress` deletes — so a record that could be read two ways is refused rather than guessed at (SPEC §2).

record.title: record
record.description: One entry of a document's `entities` array, in exactly one of its four kinds.

declaration.title: declaration
declaration.description: Introduces an entity with a freshly minted UUID — or, in a later layer, replaces components of one an earlier layer introduced, per component and wholesale (SPEC §2, §8). Writing an entity down is what mints its identity, so the `id` here is a UUID; a derivation address in this position would claim a generator produced the entity, and is refused rather than read as a UUID with an unusual spelling (SPEC §3).

patch.title: patch
patch.description: Modifies an entity some earlier layer declared, and fails the load if no such entity exists — which is why an overlay document uses patches: a mistyped UUID cannot silently mint a half-formed entity (SPEC §2). Its `id` is a declared entity's UUID, for the same reason a declaration's is; a derived entity is reached by `derivation`.

override.title: override
override.description: Replaces components of one derived entity, addressed by the generator and key that produced it. Each listed component replaces the derived one of the same name wholesale — no deep merge, so the result is predictable and diffable. An address no generator produces is a load error: a pinned cell never quietly evaporates (SPEC §3).

id.description: The identity this record addresses, spelled flat. A record may state both it and `derivation`; they are two spellings of one address, and the loader rejects a disagreement.

suppression.title: suppression
suppression.description: Deletes the addressed entity — the graph then routes around a hole, not a flag. It carries no components, and a dangling address fails the load exactly as an override's does (SPEC §2, §3). It reaches either kind: `id` names a declared entity by its UUID or a derived one by its address, and `derivation` names a derived one in the two parts a record usually writes it in.

expect.title: expect
expect.description: A geometric pin on a record that addresses an ordinal key: fail loudly if the target no longer sits where the author believed. Tiling keys are ordinal, so a pitch change can silently re-aim an address at a different patch of floor — which is why this is legal on suppressions too (SPEC §3).

position.description: Where the author believes it sits, in the steps of the frame the generator's region or pose is stated in.

tolerance.description: How far off it may be before the load fails.
